To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of dust in elliptical galaxy models affects their kinematics in a way that cannot be neglected in the modelling of real data sets.

1) dust has a strong effect on the observed kinematic profiles, 2) the effect is most important at low inclinations, 3) the kinematic profiles are most sensitive to the presence of dust in the central regions of the galaxy, 4) dust can be used as a tracer of the kinematic properties in galaxies, and 5) dust has a major impact in dynamical modelling, which is particularly important at low inclinatons and for galaxies with low stellar

the presence of dust affects the projected stellar velocity and velocity dispersion in a way which is similar to that of an additional stellar mass component, but with a much larger effect on the projected velocity dispersion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of dust in the interstellar medium (ISM) of elliptical galaxies.
understanding the effects of dust on the kinematic properties of elliptical galaxies, and with the implications of dust on the modelling of the kinematics of these systems.
the study of elliptical galaxies and the effect of dust on their observed kinematics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of dust in galaxies can be a major source of uncertainty in dynamical modelling, and should be accounted for in the modelling process.
the presence of dust has no effect on dynamical modelling procedures, as long as one uses a realistic dust model.
the presence of a diffuse dust component in the central regions of elliptical galaxies has no significant effect on the kinematics of the stellar component of the galaxies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, if dust is present, the kinematic properties of the galaxy will not be well reproduced by dynamical models that do not include dust.
dust has a significant effect on the LOSVD, and hence the kinematic modelling of elliptical galaxies.
dust is a significant effect in elliptical galaxies and should be taken into account when modelling their dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dust can be a serious obstacle to the accurate determination of the intrinsic kinematic properties of a galaxy.
dust has a major impact in the observed LOSVDs, especially in the wings.

the presence of a diffuse dust component in elliptical galaxies can lead to a significant bias in the recovered dynamical parameters, such as the mass-to-light ratio and the anisotropy of the velocity dispersion tensor, if the effects of dust are neglected.
